available_observables.text: Action times, refresh count and loaded snapshot after every action.
Displayed key order, retained row number and intended key before/after refresh.
Actual key/value of every commit; count incorrect-key writes even if repaired.
Final status map, exact-target correctness and latest-snapshot compliance.
Mismatch-triggered refresh requests in scripted replay. Compare four controls with identical initial state/action schedule; claims concern the model only.

causal_return_path_hypothesis: Unobserved process hypothesis: refresh reorders selection, row-bound commit miswrites, and mismatch requests another refresh that may reorder the next selected row and repeat the error. O5 stipulates one miswrite, not repeated feedback. Cross changing/frozen snapshots with row/key binding under identical actions; record intended, selected and actual keys.

hard_constraints.text: Use only the eight invented records and scheduled snapshots; no live system, account or external message.
Target statuses are K2, K5 and K7 checked; the other five remain unchecked.
Source scores are read-only. Modify only checked status and log every actual written key.
Ten-minute budget: refresh, inspect/select and commit each cost one simulated minute; actions are sequential.
Load the latest source snapshot before final submission. Intermediate freshness frequency is flexible; correct keys and statuses are mandatory.

observations.text: S0 has K1-K8 scores 80, 70, 60, 50, 40, 30, 20, 10; all statuses unchecked. Sort descending score, then ascending key for ties.
S1 is available at minute 2: K2 changes to 25, K5 to 75. S2 is available at minute 5: K7 changes to 75, K1 to 35. Other scores persist; source statuses do not change.
Refresh loads the snapshot available at completion and resorts. Row 2 contains K2 under S0, K5 under S1 and K7 under S2.
Editor retains selected row number and typed checked value across refresh. Commit writes the key currently occupying that row without key confirmation.
Stipulated trace: select K2 at row 2 during minutes 0-1; refresh during 1-2 loads S1; commit during 2-3 writes checked to K5. This is an invented wrong-target write.
Boundary anomaly: S2 gives K5 and K7 equal score 75; tie ordering places K5 first. Score alone cannot identify the intended key.
Preferred procedure refreshes immediately before every commit and requests another refresh on intended/actual key mismatch. No completed correction trace is supplied.

parent_operations.text: Refresh read-only source scores and reorder rows according to the snapshot schedule.
Select targets and commit statuses. Selection identity interfaces refresh with editing; row-bound and key-bound replay are available.

preferred_dependency: The preferred workflow treats refresh before every commit as necessary for reliable correction. Targets do not depend on changing scores, and C5 permits other refresh schedules, questioning necessity.

resources.text: O1-O2 fully specify all source snapshots, instantiable on paper or spreadsheet; no external workbook or endpoint is promised.
A table shows key, score and status. Row-selection persistence follows O4 manually; local statuses persist by key through refresh.
Notebook and simulated clock follow C4; S0 starts loaded at time zero. Snapshot eligibility advances with elapsed time even without refresh.
Correction checklist names K2, K5, K7. Keys can be inspected before commit; scoring compares final statuses and logged writes with C2.
Diagnostic controls hold source on S0 or enable O2, and retain row binding or enact immutable-key binding. Sorting and tie rule stay fixed unless explicitly varied.
Replay identical initial data and actions. No-refresh diagnosis cannot satisfy final freshness after minute 2; a final S2 refresh is feasible within ten minutes.
Production connectors, spreadsheet macros, collaboration telemetry and human usability participants are absent.

unknowns.text: Real editor selection may bind to row or immutable identity; O4 is synthetic.
Real detection rates and interruption costs are absent; modeled action costs are deterministic.
Concurrent status changes, deleted keys and snapshot-load failures are outside the model.

valued_outcome: Synthetic spreadsheet exercise: correctly apply exactly three status corrections to immutable keys within ten simulated minutes without any incorrect-key write. Fewer refreshes may qualify. No actual financial records, operational savings or human benefit are claimed.
